summary: First lit 1 March 1885 on North Head at the entrance to Brigus Harbour, Conception Bay. The Coast Guard still shows a white flash from its red-and-white iron tower.

lens.note: Sixth-order lens with an Argand lamp at first lighting (LighthouseFriends). Current lens not in sources.

structures.type: cylindrical cast-iron tower with lantern and gallery, red and white vertical stripes
structures.note: 9.5 m on the Coast Guard list and in LighthouseFriends; 9 m (31 ft) in the Lighthouse Directory.

structures.type: two-storey dwelling with a mansard roof, painted red and white
structures.note: Torn down after the light was electrified in 1931 (LighthouseFriends; Lighthouse Directory: demolished).

staffing.note: After 1931 the light was run from a switch near the government wharf in Brigus. No source gives the date the station became automatic.

access.note: Grounds open; tower closed. Hiking trail starts from Battery Road in Brigus and is not clearly marked. Owned by the Canadian Coast Guard.

notes_for_editor: Thin history: the 1885 to 1931 chronology rests on one source, LighthouseFriends, which cites the Journal of the House of Assembly and the 1981 Encyclopedia of Newfoundland and Labrador. Neither was read. The Marine annual reports in the corpus (1900 to 1924) have no entry for Brigus North Head; no newspaper search was run. Present-day facts (characteristic, focal height, tower height, range, status) are corroborated by the Coast Guard list and the Lighthouse Directory. Tower height disagrees: 9.5 m (Coast Guard, LighthouseFriends) against 9 m (Lighthouse Directory); the story uses 9.5 m. LighthouseFriends prints 'Water Wilcox' for the operator after 1931; the story gives the name as printed and says it may be a misprint for Walter, and no other source read names him. The light's characteristic changed from a fixed red light (1885) to a white flash, but no source dates the change. Wikipedia was not used.
